paragraphs: The door was taller than the hill, and it opened by itself. Inside, the hallway ran on for far more than two metres, under a ceiling too high for the duck's camera to focus on. Yellow Duck Sweater walked up the middle on black and white squares, cold as a plate. Each footstep came back from overhead, as if a copy were walking on the roof. Along the walls, stone kings and queens lay flat on stone beds. Fallen over, the duck thought, and never reset. It waited politely beside one. Nothing got up.

Far ahead an organ breathed in like a jet engine warming, then let out one gold note that the duck felt in its knees. Outside, the clouds moved off. The windows lit, and red and blue patches slid across the floor. The duck stepped from colour to colour and not once did it wobble. Best checkpoint yet. At the far end stood an old wooden chair, scratched all over, empty. Sitting was in its act. It climbed up, sat, and tilted its head at the empty benches. "Quack," it said, and the roof said it back eight times, a whole troupe. It stayed there with its feet sticking straight out, a square of red window resting on the knitted duckling like a medal.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck stands very small in front of a huge arched wooden door that stands open in the stone front of a great old abbey with two tall towers, under a morning sky of clouds and sun with a pale, lopsided moon. Panel 2: The duck walks up the middle of a very long, very tall stone hall with pointed arches and a black and white checkered floor, its neck bent back to look up at the faraway ceiling. Panel 3: The duck stands waiting politely beside a low stone bed on which a grey stone statue of a crowned king lies flat on its back, with a stone queen statue lying on another stone bed behind it. Panel 4: The duck stops on the checkered floor with its knees shaking a little, looking up at a wall of tall golden organ pipes that glow with warm light. Panel 5: The duck steps carefully from a red patch of light onto a blue patch of light on the checkered floor, beneath tall stained-glass windows with sunbeams slanting through them. Panel 6: The duck sits on a big, old, scratched wooden chair with a high pointed back, its orange feet sticking straight out over the edge of the seat, with a square of red light from a window resting on the knitted duckling on its sweater and rows of empty wooden benches in the dim hall behind. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
